# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ac3tests - Catch2 unit tests over ac3::forge, matroska::matroska, mp4::mp4 and
# mpegts::mpegts, plus ac3adm::ac3adm when AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM is on and ac3::sendspin when
# AC3FORGE_BUILD_HEARTH is on (see below - both are opt-in, unlike the other three). Golden
# vectors under golden/ are generated by the scripts
# in tools/ (see their headers).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Catch2 normally arrives through a package manager - vcpkg's toolchain, a
# distribution package, an explicit CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH. A fresh clone has none
# of those configured, and a test suite that disappears when the local setup is
# missing is worse than one that costs a download, so fall back to fetching it.
# The version matches the vcpkg port so both routes test against the same code.
set(AC3FORGE_CATCH2_VERSION 3.15.3)

find_package(Catch2 3 CONFIG QUIET)

if(NOT Catch2_FOUND)
    if(NOT AC3FORGE_FETCH_CATCH2)
        message(FATAL_ERROR
            "Catch2 3 was not found and AC3FORGE_FETCH_CATCH2 is OFF.\n"
            "Supply it with -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=<vcpkg>/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake "
            "or -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<prefix>, allow the download by setting "
            "AC3FORGE_FETCH_CATCH2=ON, or build without tests using "
            "-DAC3FORGE_BUILD_TESTS=OFF.")
    endif()

    message(STATUS
        "Catch2 not found locally; fetching v${AC3FORGE_CATCH2_VERSION} "
        "(-DAC3FORGE_FETCH_CATCH2=OFF to require a local copy)")

    include(FetchContent)
    FetchContent_Declare(Catch2
        GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/catchorg/Catch2.git
        GIT_TAG "v${AC3FORGE_CATCH2_VERSION}"
        GIT_SHALLOW TRUE
        # SYSTEM keeps Catch2's headers out of reach of /W4 /WX, matching how
        # the installed package presents itself; EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL keeps its
        # install rules out of ours.
        SYSTEM
        EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)
    FetchContent_MakeAvailable(Catch2)

    # catch_discover_tests() lives in Catch2's extras/. The installed package
    # config puts that directory on CMAKE_MODULE_PATH; a source build does not.
    list(APPEND CMAKE_MODULE_PATH "${catch2_SOURCE_DIR}/extras")
endif()

# -Wnull-dereference false positive, GNU only: "a rewrite really does
# re-stamp the CRCs" hand-flips one bit of an already-encoded frame
# (tampered[6] ^= std::byte{0x20}) to build its negative control, and at -O3
# (Release; not seen at the -debug preset's lower optimization) GCC inlines
# std::byte's operator^= straight into the Catch2 test body and misattributes
# a "null dereference" to the subscript - the same post-inlining
# misattribution cmake/CompilerWarnings.cmake already documents for GCC < 15
# against libstdc++ internals (see its own comment, and gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla
# PR 108757 and neighbours), surfacing here on the CI-pinned GCC 16 instead:
# confirmed on a plain WSL2 GCC 15.2.0 build (config-linux-gcc, not just
# -debug) and, for real, in CI's own build logs (CodeQL, adm-validate, and
# the plain Linux GCC/GCC-arm64 legs all hit it). `tampered` is a full copy
# of a real encoded AC-3 syncframe, always far more than 6 bytes, so nothing
# here is genuinely null-unsafe. Scoped to the file rather than widening
# that project-wide guard, the same reasoning src/ac3adm/CMakeLists.txt's
# own GCC-15 instance of this category gives for scoping to its one target:
# nothing else in this project has hit it, so silencing it everywhere would
# risk hiding a genuine one elsewhere.
set_source_files_properties(io/test_metadata_edit.cpp
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "$<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:GNU>:-Wno-null-dereference>")

# The same GNU-only false positive, in a different disguise, on the hearth
# queue tests: GCC at -O3 inlines std::operator==(const string&, const char*)
# into a CHECK that compares a title against a literal ("b"), follows it down
# to traits_type::length on the literal's pointer, and reports a null
# dereference at basic_string.h:1165. The full -Wnull-dereference chain names
# Catch2's decomposer and the literal's own type (const char (&)[2]), so the
# pointer it worries about is a string constant - never null. Restructuring
# the test away from it was tried first and changes nothing, since the
# comparison itself is what gets inlined; scoped to these two files rather
# than widened for the same reason the block above gives.
set_source_files_properties(hearth/test_queue.cpp hearth/test_transport.cpp
    PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "$<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:GNU>:-Wno-null-dereference>")

# test_signing.cpp reaches ac3::signing's internal crypto headers (sha256.hpp/
# hmac_sha256.hpp) to run the FIPS/RFC known-answer vectors directly - they are
# not part of the target's public API, so put its private src/ dir on this
# target's include path only, the same pattern the alsa backend's internal
# header uses below.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/signing/src")

# test_bit_reservoir.cpp reaches the encoder's own internal bit_reservoir.hpp
# (ABR's sliding-window accounting), which is plumbing between the encoder's
# translation units rather than library surface - same pattern, same reason.
# test_exp_strategy.cpp includes exp_strategy.hpp, the exponent-run planner the
# two encoder translation units share. It is deliberately not library surface -
# nothing outside src/forge/src/encoder/ has any business planning exponent
# runs - but what it decides is a cost judgement, and that is worth holding to
# account on inputs chosen to make the right answer obvious rather than only
# through a whole encode. Same pattern as the signing headers above.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/forge/src/encoder")

# test_scalar_math.cpp includes src/forge/src/core/scalar_math.hpp, the float
# encode path's own log2/log/exp - internal for the same reason as the
# exponent-run planner above, and worth holding to accuracy bounds on its own
# rather than only through the fixture hashes that depend on it.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/forge/src/core")
# test_block_norm.cpp includes src/forge/src/decoder/block_norm.hpp, the
# fixed-point tier's block exponent, which both decoders share and which is not
# library surface.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/forge/src/decoder")
# tests/ac4dec/test_ac4dec_{asf,metadata,presentation,channel_elements}.cpp reach the
# AC-4 decoder's syntax functions (src/ac4dec/src/syntax/) to hold each branch of
# the syntax to a hand-built bitstream - the committed streams reach only the
# branches DEE writes - and the other tests in the block below reach its PCM
# functions (src/ac4dec/src/pcm/) and the encoder's writer (src/ac4enc/src/).
# Same pattern as the forge headers above, with one difference: those headers
# are inline, and these functions are compiled into ac4dec_objects and
# ac4enc_objects under CXX_VISIBILITY_PRESET hidden. With BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON,
# ac4::decoder is libac4dec.so and ac4::encoder libac4enc.so, which export none
# of them, so these tests link only against the static libraries and are built
# only when that is what ac4::decoder and ac4::encoder name. They test the
# syntax and the arithmetic, not the linkage: every static leg runs them, and
# the shared-libs pass (config-linux-llvm-shared) still runs the tests of the
# public API, test_ac4dec_{decoder,frames,syntax}.cpp and test_ac4enc_encoder.cpp,
# against the real .so files. Linking the static libraries here instead would
# let those bind to a static copy too, and stop testing the .so files at all.
# The shared core's headers (src/ac4core/src, for tests/ac4core/ and the
# tables) come with linking ac4::core below, a static library in every build.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/ac4dec/src")
if(NOT BUILD_SHARED_LIBS)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
        ac4dec/ac4dec_constructed.cpp
        ac4dec/ac4dec_mux.cpp
        ac4dec/ac4dec_objects.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_acpl.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_asf.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_aspx.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_channel_elements.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_constructed.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_de.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_downmix.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_drc.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_immersive.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_metadata.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_multichannel.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_objects.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_pcm.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_presentation.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_presentations.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_renderer.cpp
        ac4enc/test_ac4enc_acpl.cpp
        ac4enc/test_ac4enc_aspx.cpp
        ac4enc/test_ac4enc_multichannel.cpp
        ac4enc/test_ac4enc_writer.cpp)
endif()
# tests/ac4enc/ reach the encoder's writer (src/ac4enc/src/) the same way; the
# two libraries' internal headers keep distinct names (bit_reader.hpp and
# syntax/ against bit_writer.hpp, asf/ and frame/).
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/ac4enc/src")

# test_simd_kernels.cpp (SIMD kernels) needs the ONE architecture directory
# CMake selected in src/forge/CMakeLists.txt, so the test exercises the
# f64x2/i32x4 the library was actually built with rather than a different
# one - same white-box arrangement as src/signing/src just above and the ALSA
# backend's internal header below.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${AC3FORGE_ARCH_INCLUDE_DIR}")

# The interleave and the DMA queue model from the ESP-IDF component
# (ac3forge/interleave.hpp, ac3forge/dac_queue_model.hpp). Reaching into the
# component is deliberate: they are the parts of an I2S or TDM sink that can be
# checked without a DAC on the other end - the rest is peripheral setup and a
# blocking write - and they are the parts with the indexing and the arithmetic
# in them. test_block_ring.cpp and test_unit_hold.cpp build the component's
# block_ring.hpp and unit_hold.hpp through the same path, and
# test_pairing_records.cpp the Sendspin player's record order and eviction
# (pairing_records.hpp), which the board keeps in NVS. None of these headers
# includes anything from ESP-IDF, which is what makes building them here
# possible and is worth keeping true. (The layout and the renderer were here
# too, and moved into the library as ac3/render/ with render/test_layout.cpp.)
#
# interleave.hpp also needs ac3forge/slot_conversion.hpp, which the component
# takes from conversion/float/ or conversion/bits/ by whether the part has a
# floating-point unit. A host has one, so the float directory; the tests name
# both conversions explicitly wherever the choice matters.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/esp-idf/ac3forge/include"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/esp-idf/ac3forge/conversion/float")

# test_simd_kernels.cpp's CPU-feature-detection cases (SIMD kernels's
# dynamic-dispatch follow-on) need cpu_features.cpp compiled a SECOND time,
# directly into this target, against the same resolved probe directory
# src/forge/CMakeLists.txt selected for the library - rather than calling
# into forge_objects's own copy of has_avx2(), which would need
# dllexport/dllimport treatment that would otherwise only matter for the
# config-linux-llvm-shared (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON) leg. Same white-box
# arrangement as src/signing/src above, and unconditional: has_avx2()
# correctly answering "false" on a build with no AVX2 tier is exactly as
# worth testing as it answering "true" where one exists.
target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE "${AC3FORGE_CPU_FEATURES_SOURCE}")
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
    "${AC3FORGE_CPU_FEATURES_INCLUDE_DIR}"
    "${AC3FORGE_CPU_PROBE_INCLUDE_DIR}")
if(AC3FORGE_IS_MSVC_LIKE)
    set_source_files_properties("${AC3FORGE_CPU_FEATURES_SOURCE}" PROPERTIES
        COMPILE_OPTIONS "/wd4996")
endif()

# The AVX2 kernel side of the same follow-on: avx2_probe.cpp and
# mdct_avx2.cpp compiled a second time into this target too, same reasoning
# as cpu_features.cpp just above. AC3FORGE_AVX2_INCLUDE_DIR is empty (falsy)
# whenever src/forge/CMakeLists.txt did not build the AVX2 tier at all
# (AC3FORGE_AVX2=OFF, or a non-x86_64 target) - the test sources are
# conditional on the exact same condition the library used.
#
# Which of those two worlds the test file is in used to be an
# AC3FORGE_HAVE_AVX2_TIER compile definition it asked about with an #ifdef,
# on the reasoning that tools/checks/check_platform_macros.ps1 scanned src/
# and apps/ only. That check now covers tests/ as well, and the #ifdef was
# costing more than the rule: eleven AVX2 case bodies were not PARSED at all
# on a non-x86_64 leg, so a renamed kernel or a changed signature could only
# be caught by an x86_64 run. So the answer arrives the way every other
# either/or in this repository does - core/avx2/{present,absent}/ each ship
# an avx2_tier.hpp, CMake puts the matching one on the include path, and
# ac3::test::avx2::kTierCompiled is a constexpr bool the test branches on
# with a plain `if`. The absent variant declares the same eight entry points
# and defines them as unreachable stubs (see its own header), so both arms
# compile everywhere.
if(AC3FORGE_AVX2_INCLUDE_DIR)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
        "${AC3FORGE_AVX2_INCLUDE_DIR}/avx2_probe.cpp"
        "${AC3FORGE_AVX2_INCLUDE_DIR}/mdct_avx2.cpp")
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
        "${AC3FORGE_AVX2_INCLUDE_DIR}"
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/core/avx2/present")
    if(AC3FORGE_IS_MSVC_LIKE)
        set_source_files_properties(
            "${AC3FORGE_AVX2_INCLUDE_DIR}/avx2_probe.cpp"
            "${AC3FORGE_AVX2_INCLUDE_DIR}/mdct_avx2.cpp" PROPERTIES
            COMPILE_OPTIONS "/arch:AVX2")
    else()
        set_source_files_properties(
            "${AC3FORGE_AVX2_INCLUDE_DIR}/avx2_probe.cpp"
            "${AC3FORGE_AVX2_INCLUDE_DIR}/mdct_avx2.cpp" PROPERTIES
            COMPILE_OPTIONS "-mavx2")
    endif()
else()
    # mdct_avx2.hpp too: src/forge/src/internal/avx2/none/mdct_avx2.cpp already
    # gives every kernel it declares a std::unreachable() body inside
    # forge_objects in exactly this configuration, so the absent variant reuses
    # those rather than defining a second set (which is a duplicate-symbol link
    # error, not a harmless overlap). Reaching into src/ by path is the same
    # white-box arrangement this file already uses for src/signing/src and
    # src/forge/src/{encoder,core,decoder} above.
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/core/avx2/absent"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/forge/src/internal/avx2")
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE core/avx2/absent/avx2_tier.cpp)
endif()

# core/test_simd_kernels.cpp's own AVX2_REQUIRE knob reads std::getenv too -
# same C4996 reasoning as cpu_features.cpp above - and so do
# ac4dec/test_ac4dec_syntax.cpp, for its trace and census directories,
# ac4dec/test_ac4dec_constructed.cpp, test_ac4dec_objects.cpp and
# test_ac4dec_presentations.cpp, for where to write their streams (and
# test_ac4dec_objects.cpp for Chromium's A-JOC stream), and
# ac4dec/test_ac4dec_api.cpp, for a directory of further streams to decode.
if(AC3FORGE_IS_MSVC_LIKE)
    set_source_files_properties(core/test_simd_kernels.cpp ac4dec/test_ac4dec_syntax.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_constructed.cpp ac4dec/test_ac4dec_objects.cpp ac4dec/test_ac4dec_presentations.cpp
        ac4dec/test_ac4dec_api.cpp
        PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "/wd4996")
endif()

# decoder/test_decoder.cpp's patch_bits: GCC's -O3 VRP mis-derives, only once
# that function is inlined into one specific one-bit call site (count == 1),
# that `frame`'s backing store is null ("source object is likely at address
# zero"), and fails the build under -Werror=array-bounds. `frame` is always a
# real, previously REQUIRE()'d encoded syncframe, dozens of bytes long, at
# every call site - GCC's own known false-positive class for std::vector
# subscripting after aggressive inlining, not a real bounds issue, and the
# same family as the two GCC suppressions cmake/CompilerWarnings.cmake already
# carries (see its -Wnull-dereference and -Warray-bounds entries, which state
# the general shape: post-inlining analysis misattributing an
# optimizer-introduced "impossible" path as a real access).
#
# This was a [[gnu::noinline]] on the function, behind
# `#if defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__)` - guarded rather than bare
# because MSVC's /W4 /WX treats an unrecognized attribute (C5030) as a hard
# error rather than ignoring it, confirmed in CI. Blocking inlining did remove
# the interprocedural constant-propagation path that triggers the warning, but
# it answered a compiler question in the preprocessor, which is the one thing
# this tree does not do (tools/checks/check_platform_macros.ps1, which now
# covers tests/). Naming the diagnostic here instead says the same thing more
# directly - this warning is a known false positive in this file - and says it
# where the /wd4996 entry above and every other compiler-specific flag in this
# project already live. Clang does not warn here and needs no entry.
#
# Deliberately per-source rather than on the whole target: ac3::warnings
# already turns -Warray-bounds off tree-wide for GCC >= 16, but ac3tests is
# also built by the local development loop's older GCC, where it is still on.
if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID STREQUAL "GNU")
    set_source_files_properties(decoder/test_decoder.cpp
        PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "-Wno-array-bounds")
endif()

# render/test_layout.cpp's Speaker/OutputLayout size assertions: the numbers
# are an ABI fact, written down for MSVC's ABI (which clang-cl shares) and not
# measured anywhere else, so render/abi/{msvc,unknown}/ each ship a
# speaker_abi.hpp and this puts the matching one on the include path. It was a
# `#if defined(_MSC_VER)` in the test file; see either header for what the
# guard protects and why one ABI's numbers are worth asserting at all.
if(AC3FORGE_IS_MSVC_LIKE)
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/render/abi/msvc")
else()
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/render/abi/unknown")
endif()

# core/test_crc_mutator.cpp includes fuzz/crc_mutator.hpp - the re-stamping
# half of the libFuzzer custom mutator (signing-verify fuzz walk). The mutator itself only
# builds under Clang with -fsanitize=fuzzer, but the header's
# restamp_syncframe_crcs is ordinary portable C++ over ac3::crc16 and the
# frame-size tables, and whether it produces a crc1 the decoder accepts is
# exactly the kind of thing that should be checked on every platform rather
# than inferred from a coverage number on one. Same shape as the signing/src
# include just above: a directory outside the public include tree, on this
# target's path only.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/fuzz")

# test_selfcheck.cpp and test_eac3_selfcheck.cpp run the encoder/decoder mirror check
# (ac3::verify) over the committed programme-material fixtures rather than a synthetic
# signal - the delta bit allocation state it compares only ends part-way through a frame on
# material that really does change character mid-frame, which is what made those files the
# reproduction for the bug this check exists to catch, and the Annex E tools it also
# compares (AHT gains, coupling and spectral-extension coordinates) say nothing at all on
# silence. Passed as a path rather than resolved from argv[0]: ctest runs the binary from
# the build tree, which is nowhere near the fixtures.
target_compile_definitions(ac3tests
    PRIVATE "AC3FORGE_GOLDEN_AUDIO_DIR=\"${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/golden/audio\"")

# The third-party Dolby fixture tests/oba/test_dee_joc_fixture.cpp reads, on the
# same reasoning: a path, because ctest runs from the build tree.
target_compile_definitions(ac3tests
    PRIVATE "AC3FORGE_GOLDEN_OBJECT_DIR=\"${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/golden/object-fixture\"")

# tests/ac4/test_ac4.cpp reads the real DEE-produced AC-4 fixtures under
# here (tools/generators/gen_ac4_baseline.py) - same reasoning as the two
# defines above.
target_compile_definitions(ac3tests
    PRIVATE "AC3FORGE_GOLDEN_EXTERNAL_BASELINE_DIR=\"${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/golden/external-baseline\"")

# tests/ac4dec/test_ac4dec_syntax.cpp holds the AC-4 decoder's syntax trace to
# the digests tools/references/ac4_syntax.py wrote for the same streams.
target_compile_definitions(ac3tests
    PRIVATE "AC4DEC_GOLDEN_DIR=\"${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/golden/ac4dec\"")

# crucible/test_translations.cpp reads the Crucible's six Qt Linguist
# catalogues as files (no Qt in this target), on the same reasoning: a
# source-tree path, because ctest runs the binary from the build tree.
target_compile_definitions(ac3tests
    PRIVATE "AC3FORGE_CRUCIBLE_TS_DIR=\"${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/translations\""
    # The GUI's seven catalogues are held to the same two rules as Crucible's
    # six, from the same parser. They were filled on 2026-09-06 and a rule
    # that holds them there belongs beside the one that holds Crucible's,
    # rather than in a workflow step on one leg.
    PRIVATE "AC3FORGE_GUI_TS_DIR=\"${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/gui/translations\"")

# Where every test that writes a file writes it. Each such file's own scratch_dir()
# helper appends its own leaf name under here, so the artefacts stay separated by
# subject the way their old per-subject temp directories were.
#
# The point of routing them through a define at all is the ROOT of that path.
# These used to sit under fs::temp_directory_path(), which depends on nothing but
# the machine - so two ac3tests binaries built from different checkouts of this
# repo (different worktrees, different build directories, different branches)
# shared one directory and, because the filenames underneath are fixed, could
# overwrite each other's intermediate files mid-test. What that produces is not an
# obvious collision but a test failure in whichever run lost the race, in a branch
# that has nothing to do with the change under test. CI never sees it - a runner
# has its checkout to itself - so the whole cost lands on local development, where
# building several worktrees of this repo at once is normal.
#
# Keying it to CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR gives each build tree its own, which is
# also the more useful place for it: the artefacts a failing test left behind end
# up next to the binary that wrote them rather than pooled in the machine's temp
# directory with every other build's, and `rm -rf` on a build tree takes them with
# it. Supplied the same way AC3CLI_EXE and AC3FORGE_GOLDEN_AUDIO_DIR above are.
target_compile_definitions(ac3tests
    PRIVATE "AC3FORGE_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR=\"${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/scratch\"")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Toolchain hook: keep a failing assert from opening a modal dialog that hangs
# a headless CTest run. Each directory holds the same filenames; CMake selects
# the one for the target, which is why no source file here needs an #ifdef.
# The axis is the CRT, not the OS - <crtdbg.h> ships with the MSVC runtime, so
# clang-cl needs the hook and MinGW does not - so this branches on MSVC (true
# for clang-cl too) rather than on WIN32.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(MSVC)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE crt/msvc/crt_report.cpp)
else()
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE crt/stub/crt_report.cpp)
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The test suite's own platform seam - the same shape as the CRT hook above,
# and as src/audio/src/backend/<backend>/ and apps/cli/platform/<os>/.
#
# Two things a test needs that the standard library does not portably give it:
# this process's id (for the per-process scratch leaf every writing test takes)
# and running a command with its real exit code back (std::system() returns the
# child's exit code on Windows but a raw wait() status word on POSIX, and
# cmd.exe needs a quote-wrapping that sh must not get). Both used to be written
# inline behind `#ifdef _WIN32` in nineteen and eight test files respectively.
#
# Each directory holds the same filename; CMake compiles the one for the
# target, so no test source has to ask which platform it is on - which is what
# lets tools/checks/check_platform_macros.ps1 cover tests/ as it already covers
# src/ and apps/. The axis is the OS, not the CRT, so this branches on WIN32
# rather than on MSVC: a MinGW build wants <process.h>'s _getpid() and cmd.exe's
# quoting just as much as an MSVC one does.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(WIN32)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE platform/windows/process.cpp)
else()
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE platform/posix/process.cpp)
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The audio backend's own tests, on the same axis the library selects it on.
#
# src/audio/CMakeLists.txt compiles exactly one src/backend/<backend>/ directory
# and publishes which one; a backend with device-free logic worth testing gets
# a matching tests/backend/<backend>/ directory here, added only in the build
# that compiled it. So the suite can never test a backend the library does not
# contain, and no test source needs to ask which platform it is on.
#
# test_audio_backend.cpp above is the other half and is unconditional: it holds
# the contract EVERY backend keeps, including the one that refuses everything.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND STREQUAL "alsa")
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
        backend/alsa/test_alsa_device_names.cpp
        backend/alsa/test_alsa_eld_parsing.cpp
        # Software ALSA devices (audio/alsa_null_device.hpp): the backend's
        # classes and the device-facing ac3cli commands against alsa-lib's
        # null/file/route plugins, so their success paths run without a card.
        audio/test_alsa_null_backend.cpp)
    # The backend's internal header. Not part of the library's public
    # interface and deliberately not installed - it is on the include path for
    # this target only, and only in this configuration.
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND_DIR}")
elseif(AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND STREQUAL "pipewire")
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE backend/pipewire/test_pipewire_support.cpp)
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND_DIR}")
    # test_pipewire_support.cpp includes pipewire_support.hpp directly, which
    # in turn includes PipeWire's own headers - the same PkgConfig::PipeWire
    # target src/audio/CMakeLists.txt linked ac3audio against, needed again
    # here since this is a separate translation unit in a separate target.
    target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE PkgConfig::PipeWire)
elseif(AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND STREQUAL "android")
    # Desktop-hosted ac3tests never actually selects the android backend (it
    # only exists under NDK cross-compilation, which this target is not) -
    # this branch is future-proofing should that ever change, matching the
    # alsa branch's shape exactly rather than assuming android can never
    # reach here.
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE backend/android/test_android_support.cpp)
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND_DIR}")
elseif(AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND STREQUAL "macos")
    # Unlike alsa/android above, this branch DOES run on desktop-hosted
    # ac3tests for real: src/audio/CMakeLists.txt selects macos/
    # unconditionally under APPLE, so every macOS CI leg's ac3tests build
    # compiles and runs this file.
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE backend/macos/test_macos_support.cpp)
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND_DIR}")
elseif(AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND STREQUAL "windows")
    # Like macos above, this branch runs on desktop-hosted ac3tests for real:
    # src/audio/CMakeLists.txt selects windows/ unconditionally under WIN32,
    # so every Windows CI leg's ac3tests build compiles and runs this file.
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE backend/windows/test_windows_support.cpp)
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND_DIR}")
endif()

# audio/test_live_positions.cpp needs UdpSocket (src/audio/src/net/udp_socket.hpp)
# to send itself test datagrams over real loopback - internal to ac3::audio,
# not installed, on the include path the same way a backend's own internal
# header is above (AC3FORGE_AUDIO_NET_DIR, published by src/audio/CMakeLists.txt
# next to AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND_DIR). No separate ws2_32 link is needed on
# Windows: ac3audio already carries that requirement for any static-library
# consumer, ac3tests included.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${AC3FORGE_AUDIO_NET_DIR}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ac3cli integration tests (cli/test_cli.cpp). main.cpp compiles straight into
# the ac3cli executable with everything in an anonymous namespace, so there
# is no library surface for parse_options/gather_frame/run_atmos_encode's own
# logic to link against directly - these tests instead run the real, built
# ac3cli binary as a subprocess and inspect what it actually wrote.
#
# Only added when ac3cli itself is being built (AC3FORGE_BUILD_CLI): the
# top-level CMakeLists.txt processes apps/cli before tests/, so the target
# already exists here whenever it is going to.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# cli/test_cli_live.cpp rides the same gate and the same AC3CLI_EXE: it covers
# the device-facing commands (devices/outputs/record/live/monitor), which no
# test touched at all until coverage floors measured commands/audio_io.cpp and
# commands/live_audio.cpp at 0.0% line coverage. Its cases assert what holds
# with or without an endpoint present - see that file's own header - and carry
# the [concurrency] tag, so the ThreadSanitizer leg reaches them through
# `ctest -L concurrency` (ThreadSanitizer leg).
if(TARGET ac3cli)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
        cli/test_cli.cpp cli/test_cli_ac4_decode.cpp cli/test_cli_atmos_cbi.cpp cli/test_cli_containers.cpp
        cli/test_cli_live.cpp cli/test_cli_probe.cpp cli/test_cli_stream_tools.cpp
        cli/test_cli_options.cpp cli/test_cli_synth.cpp cli/test_cli_analysis.cpp
        cli/test_cli_encode_paths.cpp cli/test_cli_stream_edges.cpp
        cli/test_cli_inspect_edges.cpp cli/test_cli_atmos_edges.cpp)
    # The same device-facing commands with a device to find: software ALSA
    # devices (audio/alsa_null_device.hpp), so only in the ALSA configuration.
    if(AC3FORGE_AUDIO_BACKEND STREQUAL "alsa")
        target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE cli/test_cli_live_alsa.cpp)
    endif()
    target_compile_definitions(ac3tests PRIVATE "AC3CLI_EXE=\"$<TARGET_FILE:ac3cli>\"")
    # cli/test_cli_probe.cpp probes the committed FFmpeg/DEE-encoded fixtures as
    # well as this encoder's own output - they exercise syntax ac3forge never
    # emits (AHT, spectral extension, and frames this decoder declines
    # outright), which is the only way to check that `probe` describes a FORMAT
    # rather than this project's dialect of it. Passed as a path for the same
    # reason AC3FORGE_GOLDEN_AUDIO_DIR is: ctest runs the binary from the build
    # tree, nowhere near the fixtures.
    target_compile_definitions(ac3tests PRIVATE
        "AC3FORGE_EXTERNAL_BASELINE_DIR=\"${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/golden/external-baseline\"")
    # cli/test_cli.cpp decodes one fuzz seed under `quiet`: the DEE-encoded
    # E-AC-3 stream a quiet decode was first seen failing on, whose report
    # carries infomdat lines that FFmpeg's encode of the same programme does
    # not. A path for the same reason AC3FORGE_EXTERNAL_BASELINE_DIR is one.
    target_compile_definitions(ac3tests PRIVATE
        "AC3FORGE_FUZZ_SEED_DIR=\"${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/fuzz/seeds\"")
endif()

# RecordingSink (gui/test_recording_sink.cpp) is deliberately Qt-free - std::
# and the container libraries only, exactly so its streamed-equals-one-shot
# contract can be held here, in the plain Catch2 suite, without a QML engine
# in the room (apps/gui's Qt Quick tests cover the interactive surfaces; this
# covers the bytes). Its sources compile straight into this target the same
# way cli/test_cli.cpp's subject rides its own binary: there is no library
# surface to link against. The fragmented-MP4 cases exercise Fmp4FolderWriter,
# RecordingSink's own kFmp4 backend, so its source comes along too.
#
# Ungated since wide-layout record/live paths moved both to apps/common: both front ends write
# their takes through them now, so the bytes they produce are worth checking
# in a CLI-only build too - and apps/common, unlike apps/gui, is present
# whatever AC3FORGE_BUILD_GUI says. The test file itself stays under
# tests/gui/ so its history and its "[gui]" tag are unbroken.
#
# container_input.cpp (container readers (mkv/mp4/ts)) joined the same way for the same reason:
# ac3::apps::sniff_container/elementary_stream_from_bytes are what
# decode/qc/levels/play/monitor and the GUI's QC/Inspect pickers all call, so
# a sniffing regression belongs in the plain Catch2 suite rather than only in
# the Python encoder-space fuzzer that first found one (REGRESSION_SEEDS'
# 3600083275727211684 in tools/ci/fuzz_encoder_space.py) - this file covers it
# deterministically and without needing ffmpeg on the machine running it.
# stream_playback.cpp joined for the reason its own header gives: 'monitor'
# and 'spatial' pick their decoder and drain the end-of-stream flush through
# it, and neither command reaches its decode loop without a render device, so
# decoder/test_stream_playback.cpp holds both here instead. sink_wait.hpp is
# header-only and here for the same reason: 'play', 'monitor', 'identify' and
# 'live' wait on their sinks through it, and audio/test_sink_wait.cpp holds
# those waits against sinks that stop on cue.
# ac3gui's diagnostics module (apps/gui/gui_diagnostics.hpp) rides the same
# target for the same reason and with the same discipline: it is Qt-free, so
# the rule it exists to hold - the support file carries no signing key, no
# environment value and no byte of a loaded source - is checked on every CI
# leg, including the ones that build no window. The window's Qt Quick suite
# covers the other half, that the controller fills the report's fields from
# what the window is actually showing. The file carries a gui_ prefix because
# this target also compiles the Crucible's own diagnostics.cpp and has both
# directories on its include path.
target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
    gui/test_recording_sink.cpp
    gui/test_gui_diagnostics.cpp
    decoder/test_stream_playback.cpp
    audio/test_sink_wait.cpp
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/common/fmp4_folder_writer.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/common/recording_sink.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/common/container_input.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/common/stream_playback.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/gui/gui_diagnostics.cpp")
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/common"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/gui")

# AC3Forge Crucible's engine core (WASAPI loopback tap/UX12, apps/crucible/
# engine/): the slot plan, the bed mixer, placement smoothing and the
# output-mode policy. All four are plain C++ over ac3::oba types with no
# platform in them - the platform layer next to them is what talks to WASAPI
# or PipeWire - so they compile into this target on every platform, ungated,
# the same way apps/common does above: the rules the window's UI hangs on
# are worth holding on a CI leg that does not build the window itself. The
# app target (AC3FORGE_BUILD_CRUCIBLE, Windows and Linux) is separate.
#
# The tap pool and the output stage joined them once they were written over
# the AudioDevices seam (apps/crucible/engine/audio_devices.hpp): with the
# WASAPI classes behind an interface they are plain C++ over the library's
# codec, packer and decoder, and tests/crucible/fake_devices.hpp stands in
# for the machine. platform_audio_devices() itself is declared in
# platform_services.hpp and defined in
# apps/crucible/engine/library_devices.cpp, which this target does not
# compile; these tests never call it, and the one place the stage would
# (a null `devices` in its config) is a path the tests do not take, so the
# reference resolves to the stub below on every platform and to the real
# thing in the app.
#
# engine.cpp itself joined them last, with signing_hook.cpp beside it because
# the frame loop owns a SigningHook. It is the same argument one step up: the
# loop is written over the three seams EngineConfig injects (devices,
# sessions, foreground), so with fakes in all three it runs here as plain C++
# on any platform - and until crucible/test_engine.cpp nothing in the suite
# constructed an Engine at all, which is how a probe thread that was never
# joined reached a released branch. That file also asserts what the loop does
# about opening taps: the platform seams it would otherwise reach for are the
# ones platform_services_stub.cpp answers, and every case passes fakes
# instead. The one platform piece it does touch is ac3::audio's DeviceWatcher,
# which is linked below and answers with kNoBackend where there is none; the
# engine notes that and carries on.
#
# crucible/test_engine_start.cpp rides the same block for what start()
# answers: that a machine with nothing to play into is refused rather than
# reported as running, which is what the window's status strip prints and
# what the QML suites' "the engine did not start here" skips test for.
target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
    crucible/test_slots.cpp
    crucible/test_bed_mixer.cpp
    crucible/test_placement.cpp
    crucible/test_output_policy.cpp
    crucible/test_tap_pool.cpp
    crucible/test_output_stage.cpp
    crucible/test_engine_start.cpp
    crucible/test_nullsink_position.cpp
    crucible/test_platform_seams.cpp
    crucible/test_diagnostics.cpp
    crucible/test_desktop_entries.cpp
    crucible/test_translations.cpp
    crucible/test_engine.cpp
    crucible/test_engine_commands.cpp
    crucible/test_output_stage_edges.cpp
    crucible/platform_services_stub.cpp
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/slots.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/bed_mixer.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/placement.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/output_policy.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/tap_pool.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/diagnostics.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/output_stage.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/signing_hook.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/engine.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/ui/desktop_entries.cpp")
# test_engine_commands.cpp saves the signing key's env-var fallbacks with
# std::getenv before clearing them for its own case - same C4996 reasoning as
# src/signing/src/signing_key.cpp (src/signing/CMakeLists.txt) and
# core/test_simd_kernels.cpp above.
if(AC3FORGE_IS_MSVC_LIKE)
    set_source_files_properties(crucible/test_engine_commands.cpp
        PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "/wd4996")
endif()
# The null-sink driver's position clock (apps/windows/driver/Source/Main/
# position.h) is a header with no kernel dependencies, kept that way so the
# one piece of the driver that is logic rather than framework plumbing is
# tested here, on every platform, where kernel code could never be. The
# window's .desktop-entry reader (apps/crucible/ui/desktop_entries.hpp) is
# plain C++ over std::filesystem for the same reason and rides the same
# target, Qt-free, on every platform.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/ui"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/windows/driver/Source/Main")
# The profiling header pair, for engine.cpp's Tracy zones: the same
# generator expression apps/crucible/CMakeLists.txt uses for
# ac3crucible_engine, and for the same reason - the header is PRIVATE to
# forge_objects, so a target that includes it says so itself rather than
# picking it up from ac3::forge. Which of the two identically-pathed
# variants is chosen is CMake's decision, never an #ifdef.
target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
    "$<IF:$<BOOL:${AC3FORGE_ENABLE_TRACY}>,${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/forge/src/internal/profiling/tracy_enabled,${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/forge/src/internal/profiling/tracy_disabled>")
target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE ac3::tracy)

# The Linux Foreground's X11 half has a pure policy (x11_foreground.cpp: when
# a read yields a pid, when a lost display becomes a reason) over an injected
# reader, and the session classification and the process-tree walk beside it
# are headers. None of it needs xcb or a display, so it is tested here with a
# fake reader - on Linux only, the way tests/backend/pipewire rides its
# backend: the files live in a platform directory and are compiled nowhere
# else. Ungated on AC3FORGE_BUILD_CRUCIBLE for the reason the block above
# gives: the rules are worth holding on a leg that never builds the app.
#
# test_session_facts.cpp rides the same block for the same reason, and is why
# proc_facts.hpp exists: the Linux session monitor's /proc readers, its
# per-process fact cache and the two records a refresh builds were all inside
# session_monitor.cpp, which cannot be compiled at all without the PipeWire
# headers - so none of it could be reached from here. Moved into a header
# beside it, none of it needs PipeWire and all of it runs on any Linux
# machine, against a /proc the test writes itself. Unlike x11_foreground.cpp
# below, no file from apps/crucible is added beside it: the header is compiled
# into this case, and the .cpp that includes it stays in ac3crucible_engine
# where libpipewire is.
if(LINUX)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
        crucible/platform/linux/test_x11_foreground.cpp
        crucible/platform/linux/test_session_facts.cpp
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/platform/linux/x11_foreground.cpp")
    target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/crucible/engine/platform/linux")
endif()

# ac3adm::ac3adm is opt-in (AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM, default OFF - see the root CMakeLists.txt's own
# option() for why it is not on by default like matroska/mp4/mpegts) - test_adm.cpp is only
# added, and ac3adm::ac3adm only linked, when that option turned this target on. Unlike cli/test_cli.cpp
# above this can't key off TARGET ac3adm::ac3adm existing, since that alias is only defined
# inside src/ac3adm/CMakeLists.txt's own add_subdirectory(), which never runs unless
# AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM is already ON - so the option itself is what's checked here instead.
#
# test_adm_bridge.cpp (ac3::admbridge, ADM BWF reader phase 2, src/admbridge) rides the same gate:
# it depends on ac3adm::ac3adm too, and src/admbridge is only add_subdirectory()'d from inside
# the same if(AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM) block in the root CMakeLists.txt.
if(AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE adm/test_adm.cpp admbridge/test_adm_bridge.cpp
                                    admbridge/test_adm_bridge_write.cpp
                                    admbridge/test_iab_bridge.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE ac3adm::ac3adm ac3::admbridge)
endif()

# test_cli_atmos_adm.cpp (ADM BWF reader phase 3, ac3cli's 'atmos-adm' command) needs BOTH conditions
# above to hold at once, not just AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM alone: it runs the real, built ac3cli binary
# as a subprocess (AC3CLI_EXE, defined only inside the `if(TARGET ac3cli)` block above) against an
# ADM fixture, so the command it exercises only exists in that binary at all when
# AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM was ALSO on for this same configure (apps/cli/CMakeLists.txt's own
# AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM guard). Neither `if(TARGET ac3cli)` alone (AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM could be off,
# and 'atmos-adm' simply would not exist in that binary) nor `if(AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM)` alone
# (AC3CLI_EXE might not be defined at all, e.g. AC3FORGE_BUILD_CLI=OFF) is sufficient by itself -
# both are checked together here, after both blocks above have already run.
if(AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM AND TARGET ac3cli)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE cli/test_cli_atmos_adm.cpp cli/test_cli_atmos_iab.cpp
                                    cli/test_cli_decode_adm.cpp)
endif()

# ac3iab::ac3iab (IAB reader phase 1, src/ac3iab) is gated by its own AC3FORGE_BUILD_IAB
# (default ON, see the root CMakeLists.txt's own option()) rather than being linked
# unconditionally in the matroska::matroska/mp4::mp4/mpegts::mpegts list below - nothing else
# in this test binary depends on it, so there is no FATAL_ERROR guard forcing the option to
# stay on the way there is for those three; test_ac3iab.cpp is only added, and ac3iab::ac3iab
# only linked, when AC3FORGE_BUILD_IAB actually turned the target on. Same conditional shape
# as the AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM block above.
if(AC3FORGE_BUILD_IAB)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE ac3iab/test_ac3iab.cpp ac3iab/test_ac3iab_truncation.cpp ac3iab/test_mxf_reader.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE ac3iab::ac3iab)
endif()

# iamf::iamf (IAMF writer phase 1, src/iamf) is gated by its own AC3FORGE_BUILD_IAMF (default ON,
# see the root CMakeLists.txt's own option()), same conditional shape as the AC3FORGE_BUILD_IAB
# block immediately above.
if(AC3FORGE_BUILD_IAMF)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE iamf/test_iamf.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE iamf::iamf)
endif()

# ac3::forge_c is an optional component (AC3FORGE_BUILD_CAPI, default ON - see the root
# CMakeLists.txt) - test_capi.cpp (C API) only exists to build when it was actually built,
# the same shape as the AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM-gated sources above.
if(AC3FORGE_BUILD_CAPI)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE capi/test_capi.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE ac3::forge_c)
endif()

# ac3::sendspin (src/sendspin) is opt-in through AC3FORGE_BUILD_HEARTH, the same shape as the
# AC3FORGE_BUILD_ADM block above.
if(AC3FORGE_BUILD_HEARTH)
    # The engine (apps/hearth/engine) comes first because it needs nothing from
    # src/sendspin's player half: a core-only build still builds and tests it,
    # unlike the test sink further down.
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
        hearth/test_ac3_transcoder.cpp
        hearth/test_decoder_settings.cpp
        hearth/test_diagnostics.cpp
        hearth/test_engine.cpp
        hearth/test_engine_queue_commands.cpp
        hearth/test_media_info.cpp
        hearth/test_media_info_json.cpp
        hearth/test_network_view.cpp
        hearth/test_output_decision.cpp
        hearth/test_output_selector.cpp
        hearth/test_play_meters.cpp
        hearth/test_player.cpp
        hearth/test_player_bitstream.cpp
        hearth/test_queue.cpp
        hearth/test_session.cpp
        hearth/test_settings_model.cpp
        hearth/test_stream_decoder.cpp
        hearth/test_transport.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE ac3hearth_engine)

    # ac3hearth_controller_tests - Catch2 coverage for hearth_controller.cpp's
    # QML-translation layer (issue #886, part 2: queue_row(), media_info_to_map()
    # and friends - see tests/hearth/test_hearth_controller.cpp's own header for
    # the full rationale). A SEPARATE small binary rather than folding into
    # ac3tests above: ac3tests is Qt-free by design (see gui_diagnostics.cpp's
    # and the Crucible engine sources' own comments elsewhere in this file), and
    # hearth_controller.cpp needs Qt Core (QVariantMap/QString) plus a
    # QObject-derived class that also touches Qt Gui/Qml - never Quick,
    # QuickControls2 or Widgets, and never a live QGuiApplication instance.
    # Gated on AC3FORGE_SENDSPIN_CORE_ONLY the same way apps/hearth/CMakeLists.txt
    # itself gates add_subdirectory(ui): apps/hearth/ui does not exist at all
    # under that build (its own comment: the window "needs more than [the] core"),
    # so there is nothing here to compile against. find_package() is called
    # directly rather than reusing apps/hearth/ui/CMakeLists.txt's own
    # AC3HEARTH_UI_QT_FOUND: that PARENT_SCOPE variable stops at
    # apps/hearth/CMakeLists.txt's own scope (it is never re-exported past that
    # one level), so it does not reach this file's scope as a plain variable read.
    if(NOT AC3FORGE_SENDSPIN_CORE_ONLY)
        find_package(Qt6 6.8 QUIET COMPONENTS Core Gui Qml)
        if(Qt6_FOUND)
            add_executable(ac3hearth_controller_tests
                hearth/test_hearth_controller.cpp
                "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/hearth/ui/hearth_controller.hpp"
                "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/hearth/ui/item_loader.cpp"
                "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/hearth/ui/item_loader.hpp"
                "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/common/container_input.cpp"
                "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/common/container_input.hpp")
            # hearth_controller.cpp itself is NOT listed as a source: it is
            # #include'd directly by test_hearth_controller.cpp (that file's own
            # header explains why - internal-linkage functions with no header to
            # declare them), so listing it here too would compile it twice and
            # fail at link time with duplicate HearthController symbols. AUTOMOC
            # still needs ON to satisfy the QObject vtable HearthController's
            # methods pull in once compiled (even though no test here ever
            # constructs one) - CMake's dependency scan finds hearth_controller.hpp
            # transitively through the #include chain from the listed .cpp/.hpp
            # sources above.
            set_target_properties(ac3hearth_controller_tests PROPERTIES AUTOMOC ON)
            target_include_directories(ac3hearth_controller_tests PRIVATE
                "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/hearth/ui"
                "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/apps/common")
            target_link_libraries(ac3hearth_controller_tests PRIVATE
                ac3hearth_engine
                matroska::matroska mp4::mp4 mpegts::mpegts
                ac3::warnings ac3::fmt ac3::coverage
                Qt6::Core Qt6::Gui Qt6::Qml
                Catch2::Catch2WithMain)
            # Windows only: this target links Qt6 as shared libraries
            # (Qt6Core(d).dll etc.) with nothing of its own to put them next
            # to it, and CMake's global RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY (set at the
            # repo root - every test/CLI executable lands in a flat bin/,
            # windows-native-build-incantation's own finding) puts this exe
            # there alongside ac3hearth.exe, whose own POST_BUILD windeployqt
            # step (apps/hearth/ui/CMakeLists.txt) already deploys exactly
            # those DLLs into that same directory. Depending on ac3hearth
            # here reuses that existing deployment rather than adding a
            # second windeployqt pass - real fix for a real, reproduced
            # failure: catch_discover_tests()'s own POST_BUILD test-listing
            # step launched this exe before any Qt DLL had been deployed
            # anywhere near it and got Windows' STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND
            # (0xc0000135), which read as "Error listing tests from
            # executable" with no further detail.
            if(WIN32 AND TARGET ac3hearth)
                add_dependencies(ac3hearth_controller_tests ac3hearth)
            endif()
            # Same rationale as apps/gui/tests/CMakeLists.txt's identical loop:
            # Qt's generated moc output for THIS target compiles under the
            # strict warning set unless excluded.
            get_target_property(AC3HEARTH_CTRLTEST_SOURCES ac3hearth_controller_tests SOURCES)
            set(AC3HEARTH_CTRLTEST_GENERATED_SOURCES "")
            foreach(source IN LISTS AC3HEARTH_CTRLTEST_SOURCES)
                if(source MATCHES "^${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/.*\\.(cpp|cxx|cc)$")
                    list(APPEND AC3HEARTH_CTRLTEST_GENERATED_SOURCES "${source}")
                endif()
            endforeach()
            if(AC3HEARTH_CTRLTEST_GENERATED_SOURCES)
                set_source_files_properties(${AC3HEARTH_CTRLTEST_GENERATED_SOURCES}
                    PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "${AC3_WARNINGS_OFF_FLAG}")
            endif()
            # include(Catch) itself only happens much further down this file
            # (right before ac3tests's own catch_discover_tests() call), so
            # this block - defined well before that point - needs its own
            # copy. Harmless to include twice: CMake modules are idempotent,
            # and the later include(Catch) for ac3tests still runs unchanged.
            include(Catch)
            catch_discover_tests(ac3hearth_controller_tests ADD_TAGS_AS_LABELS)
        else()
            message(STATUS "Qt6 not found: ac3hearth_controller_tests (hearth_controller.cpp coverage) is skipped")
        endif()
    endif()

    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
        sendspin/test_ac3forge_player.cpp
        sendspin/test_arbiter.cpp
        sendspin/test_base64.cpp
        sendspin/test_base64url.cpp
        sendspin/test_chunks.cpp
        sendspin/test_clock_sync.cpp
        sendspin/test_discovery.cpp
        sendspin/test_frames.cpp
        sendspin/test_handshake.cpp
        sendspin/test_json.cpp
        sendspin/test_messages.cpp
        sendspin/test_pairing_messages.cpp
        sendspin/test_state_roles.cpp
        sendspin/test_stream_roles.cpp
        sendspin/test_transport.cpp)
    # The parts that need vcpkg's "hearth" feature, which AC3FORGE_SENDSPIN_CORE_ONLY leaves out.
    if(NOT AC3FORGE_SENDSPIN_CORE_ONLY)
        target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
            sendspin/test_codec.cpp
            sendspin/test_cpace.cpp
            sendspin/test_crypto.cpp
            sendspin/test_handshake_session.cpp
            sendspin/test_mdns.cpp
            sendspin/test_noise.cpp
            sendspin/test_pairing.cpp
            sendspin/test_pairing_flow.cpp
            sendspin/test_pairing_flow_errors.cpp
            sendspin/test_session_driver.cpp
            sendspin/test_sessions.cpp)
        # test_mdns.cpp reads the mdns backend's packet layer, which is private to the library.
        target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../src/sendspin/src")
        # test_websocket.cpp writes a WebSocket client's bytes by hand through cpp-httplib's socket
        # functions, so it is compiled on its own with cpp-httplib configured as src/sendspin
        # configures it (ac3sendspin_httplib), leaving the rest of the suite's flags alone.
        add_library(ac3tests_websocket OBJECT sendspin/test_websocket.cpp)
        target_link_libraries(ac3tests_websocket
            PRIVATE ac3::sendspin ac3sendspin_httplib ac3::warnings ac3::coverage Catch2::Catch2)
        target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE ac3tests_websocket)
        # Hearth's test sink, run in process (apps/hearth/testsink), the server's half of A4's
        # exit with aiosendspin 9.1.1 (tools/sendspin/aiosendspin_exit.py), and A6's own
        # (tools/sendspin/aiosendspin_group_exit.py) - a group with the scripted player as one
        # of its members, played from the app's own Engine.
        target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
            hearth/test_aiosendspin.cpp
            hearth/test_aiosendspin_group.cpp
            hearth/test_group.cpp
            hearth/test_testsink.cpp
            hearth/test_testsink_edges.cpp)
        # The engine's pairing records, its Network page bookkeeping (A6), its
        # NetworkGroupSink (A6, streaming to a group) and issue #874's own
        # exit - a group of two test sinks played from ac3::hearth::Engine
        # itself - all of which need src/sendspin's server half, which a
        # core-only build leaves out.
        target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE
            hearth/test_pairing_store.cpp
            hearth/test_network_sinks.cpp
            hearth/test_network_sinks_rows.cpp
            hearth/test_network_live.cpp
            hearth/test_server_host_dialling.cpp
            hearth/test_server_identity.cpp
            hearth/test_network_group_sink.cpp
            hearth/test_engine_network_group.cpp)
        target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE ac3hearth_testsink)
        # test_aiosendspin.cpp takes the player's address from std::getenv - same C4996 reasoning
        # as core/test_simd_kernels.cpp's. test_aiosendspin_group.cpp's own environment() helper
        # takes the same address the same way, and test_network_live.cpp its sinks' names.
        if(AC3FORGE_IS_MSVC_LIKE)
            set_source_files_properties(
                hearth/test_aiosendspin.cpp hearth/test_aiosendspin_group.cpp hearth/test_network_live.cpp
                PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "/wd4996")
        endif()
    endif()
    target_link_libraries(ac3tests PRIVATE ac3::sendspin)
endif()

target_include_directories(ac3tests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}")

target_link_libraries(ac3tests
    PRIVATE
        ac3::forge
        ac3::audio
        ac3::signing
        matroska::matroska
        mp4::mp4
        mpegts::mpegts
        ac4::ac4
        ac4::core
        ac4::decoder
        ac4::encoder
        ac3::warnings
        ac3::coverage
        ac3::fmt
        Catch2::Catch2WithMain)

# core/test_fixed32_ecpl.cpp calls the fixed-point tier's enhanced-coupling
# functions, which are internal to the library: declared under src/forge/src/
# rather than in the installed include tree, and so not exported from
# libac3forge.so. With BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON there is nothing for it to link
# against, and linking the static archive in as well would put a second copy of
# the codec in the executable that the shared pass exists to keep out. It tests
# the tier's arithmetic, not the linkage, and every static leg runs it.
if(NOT BUILD_SHARED_LIBS)
    target_sources(ac3tests PRIVATE core/test_fixed32_ecpl.cpp)
endif()

include(Catch)

# ADD_TAGS_AS_LABELS turns each case's Catch2 tags into ctest LABELS, which is
# what lets `ctest -L concurrency` select a subset of this one binary without
# a second discovery pass, a duplicated registration, or a name-based -R guess
# that a renamed test would silently drop out of.
#
# The label that matters today is `concurrency`: tests/audio/ (the lock-free
# SPSC ring, the silence watchdog, the clock-drift servo and the backend
# contract), cli/test_cli_live.cpp (the commands that actually start the
# capture and render threads) and crucible/test_engine.cpp (the Crucible
# engine's three threads - the frame loop, the session monitor and the probe
# - over three mutexes, four atomics and an OutputStage, including one
# deliberately unlocked read-then-take of the probe's arming flags). It is what
# CMakePresets.json's test-linux-llvm-tsan preset runs - see
# .github/workflows/_build.yml's ThreadSanitizer matrix entry and
# cmake/Sanitizers.cmake.
#
# crucible/test_engine_start.cpp drives the same engine and is deliberately
# NOT tagged: its cases assert that frames flow within two seconds, an upper
# bound on how long the engine may take, and TSan's shadow memory would break
# it. Widening that bound until it survived would delete what those cases
# check. test_engine.cpp's own waits are the other kind - a lower bound on
# stop(), and polls whose limit a slow run only approaches, never needs.
#
# The tag is on some single-threaded cases too (the resampler's own maths, the
# watchdog's clock arithmetic), deliberately: the label marks what
# ThreadSanitizer should be watching, and the types those cases exercise are
# the ones that cross the audio-thread boundary in production. A new test
# added to tests/audio/ inherits the leg by inheriting the tag.
#
# Every other tag in the suite becomes a label too, which costs nothing and
# makes `ctest -L encoder` and friends work for free.
catch_discover_tests(ac3tests ADD_TAGS_AS_LABELS)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ac3perf - real-time throughput regression guards, deliberately a SEPARATE
# binary/target from ac3tests rather than a couple more source files added to
# it. A throughput assertion is a different kind of check from the rest of
# the suite: environment-sensitive (see test_performance.cpp's ASan slack),
# meant to be read as a number as much as a pass/fail, and not something a
# quick correctness-only run (`ctest -E Performance`, say) should have to
# carry. Catch2 is already resolved above; this target just reuses it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_subdirectory(performance)
